newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan surplus unlikely to grow drastically - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan surplus unlikely to grow drastically - MITI.

text.p: The surplus in Japan's goods and services trade is not expected to increase by a large amount, although there may be temporary fluctuations from time to time, International Trade and Industry (MITI) Minister Shinji Sato said on Monday.

"The surplus in Japan's trade and services balance is not expected to increase to any great extent, although there may be temporary fluctuations," Sato said in a speech to the Foreign Correspondents' Club of Japan.
He said it was the trade and services balance, rather than overall current account data, that influences other countries. The trade and services balance is a component of the current account figure.

He said the surplus in goods and services trade accounted for only 0.2 percent of gross domestic product, and that the penetration of imported goods into the Japanese market had steadily risen in the 1990s in line with economic structural changes.
